neighbours.label: ' to' that opens an infinitive modifying a time, place or evaluation word (our time to, the wrong place to, not okay to), as against ' to' after a verb (want to, went to the store to)
fire: For the farmers, harvest is the busiest time to hire extra help.
A crowded train is a terrible place to read a long novel.
This is the best season to plant tulip bulbs in the garden.
Honestly, it's not fair to blame the new intern for that.
The library is a good place to study before exams.
Retirement is a perfect time to learn a new instrument.
It is not polite to interrupt your grandmother at dinner.
A dark alley is the worst place to wait for a taxi.
quiet: For the farmers, the owners decided to hire extra help.
On the crowded train he started to read a long novel.
This season we hope to plant tulip bulbs in the garden.
Honestly, the manager refused to blame the new intern for that.
Before exams she goes to the library every day.
After retiring he began to learn a new instrument.
The children promised to stop interrupting their grandmother.
He walked down a dark alley and waited for a taxi.
